sse.additional prompts: Do not scrape ion conductors that transport anything other than lithium. Always fill the 'Name' field using the reported name, formula, sample label, or composition; if the paper only reports a formula, use that formula as the name. If the paper is talking about a result from a previous paper, don't report that result.

Impurity phases.prompt: Impurity phases (if water impurities are present, make sure to report them)

Compound class.prompt: Compound class (Examples of these are halides, oxides, sulfides, nitrides and polymers. If multiple classes apply, report both. Do not classify polymers such as PEO as oxides. Do not classify Sulfates as Sulfides and Oxides.)

Room temperature ionic conductivity.prompt: Room temperature ionic conductivity (provide the value taken closest to room temperature)

Ionic conductivity.prompt: Ionic conductivity (if multiple measurements were taken, provide a list separated by commas)

Crystal density.prompt: Crystal density (Do not confuse this with % packing density)

Particle size.prompt: Particle size (not to be confused with grain size)

Grain size.prompt: Grain size (not to be confused with particle size)

Cell format.prompt: Cell format or measurement cell configuration, such as blocking electrode, Li/SSE/Li symmetric cell, full cell, pellet, or thin film

Pellet density.prompt: Pellet density (Do not confuse this with % packing density)

Measurement method.prompt: Measurement method used for conductivity or electrochemical measurements, such as EIS, DC polarization, Hebb-Wagner polarization, chronoamperometry, or galvanostatic cycling

Synthesis conditions.example: Ball milled, Calcined at 850 C, Sintered at 1180 C

Type of study.prompt: Type of study (experimental, computational, or both)

Atmosphere or stability condition.prompt: Atmosphere, exposure, or stability testing condition, such as dry air, humid air, argon, oxygen, water exposure, or storage duration

Specific surface area.prompt: Specific surface area, usually BET surface area. Do not confuse this with geometric contact area.

polymer.additional prompts:
Always fill the 'Name' field using the reported polymer name, sample label, grade, or trade name; if the paper only reports an abbreviation such as PLA or PHBV, use that abbreviation as the name.
Return one record per distinct polymer sample. Treat different comonomer compositions, blend ratios, molecular weight grades, filler loadings, and processing or degradation conditions as distinct entries.
If the paper is talking about a result from a previous paper, don't report that result.
Line notation rules. These apply to the 'Polymer SMILES', 'Monomer SMILES', 'BigSMILES', and 'Other structure identifier' fields:
- Only report a string that is printed as literal text in the paper, its tables, its figure captions, or its supporting information. Copy it character for character, including brackets, asterisks, dollar signs, angle brackets, and stereochemistry markers.
- Never write a structure string from your own chemical knowledge. Knowing the structure of a named polymer such as polyethylene, polystyrene, PET, or PLA is not evidence that this paper printed it.
- A drawn chemical structure, reaction scheme, or skeletal formula is not a line notation. Do not read a drawing and write it out as SMILES or BigSMILES.
- Never convert between notations. Do not turn a SMILES string into a BigSMILES string, do not turn a BigSMILES string into a SMILES string, and do not expand, canonicalize, or reformat a printed string.
- Do not repair, complete, or tidy a string that looks wrong or truncated. Copy it as printed.
- Most papers print no line notation at all. 'None' is the correct and expected answer for these fields, and reporting 'None' is never a failure.
Biodegradation rules:
- Only report degradation results that come from an experiment or an explicit claim in this paper. Do not report a material as biodegradable because polymers of its chemical class usually are.
- Keep reported test conditions with the test they belong to. If the paper reports several degradation tests for the same material in different media, return one record per test.
- Report percentage biodegradation, mass loss, and molecular weight loss in their own fields. Do not copy the same number into more than one of them.

Name.prompt: Name of the polymer as reported, including any sample label, grade, or trade name

Polymer class.prompt: Polymer class or backbone chemistry, such as polyester, polyamide, polyolefin, polycarbonate, polyurethane, polysaccharide, polypeptide, polyether, or vinyl polymer. If more than one class applies, report each.

Monomers.prompt: Monomer or comonomer names used to make the polymer, exactly as reported

Repeat unit.prompt: Description of the repeat unit as reported in words or as a chemical formula. Do not report a line notation here.

Copolymer type and composition.prompt: Copolymer architecture and comonomer composition, such as homopolymer, random, alternating, block, or graft, together with the reported comonomer ratio or blend ratio

Polymer architecture.prompt: Chain architecture, such as linear, branched, star, comb, crosslinked, network, or dendritic

Tacticity.prompt: Tacticity or stereochemistry as reported, such as isotactic, syndiotactic, atactic, or the reported D/L or R/S content

End groups.prompt: Chain end groups, or the initiator or terminating agent that defines them

Additives fillers and blends.prompt: Additives, plasticizers, fillers, compatibilizers, reinforcements, or blend partners present in the sample, with loading when reported

Synthesis method.prompt: Polymerization or processing method and conditions, such as ring-opening polymerization, polycondensation, RAFT, ATRP, melt extrusion, solvent casting, or electrospinning, including catalyst, temperature, and time when reported

Polymer SMILES.prompt: SMILES string for the polymer or its repeat unit, copied exactly as it is printed as text in the paper or its supporting information, including any * or [*] attachment points. Only report a SMILES string that is printed as text. If none is printed, report None.

Monomer SMILES.prompt: SMILES strings for the monomers, copied exactly as they are printed as text in the paper or its supporting information. Only report SMILES strings that are printed as text. If none is printed, report None.

BigSMILES.prompt: BigSMILES string copied exactly as it is printed as text in the paper or its supporting information. BigSMILES uses stochastic objects in curly braces with bonding descriptors, for example {[][$]CC[$][]}. Only report a BigSMILES string that is printed as text. Never build, complete, or convert one from a SMILES string, a drawn structure, a formula, or a polymer name. If none is printed, report None.

Other structure identifier.prompt: Any other machine-readable structure identifier printed in the paper, such as an InChI, InChIKey, CAS Registry Number, PubChem CID, or PolyInfo identifier, copied exactly as printed

Degree of polymerization.prompt: Degree of polymerization or reported average number of repeat units per chain

Degree of crystallinity.prompt: Degree of crystallinity, usually from DSC or XRD

Decomposition temperature.prompt: Thermal decomposition or degradation onset temperature from TGA. Do not confuse this with the melting temperature or with biodegradation results.

Tensile strength.prompt: Tensile strength or stress at break

Biodegradability.prompt: What the paper itself states about the biodegradability, compostability, or bio-based origin of this material, using the paper's own wording. Only report a statement the paper makes about this material. If the paper makes no such statement, report None.
Biodegradability.example: Reported as biodegradable under industrial composting conditions

Biodegradation test standard.prompt: Standard test method or protocol used for the degradation test, such as ISO 14855, ISO 17556, ISO 14851, ASTM D6400, ASTM D5988, ASTM D6691, OECD 301B, or EN 13432, copied exactly as named

Degradation medium.prompt: Medium or environment used for the degradation test, such as industrial compost, home compost, soil, seawater, marine sediment, activated sludge, freshwater, phosphate buffer, or simulated body fluid, including the reported temperature and pH

Biodegradation extent.prompt: Percentage biodegradation or mineralization reached in the test, usually evolved CO2 as a percentage of theoretical. Report the highest value reported for this material and test.

Biodegradation test duration.prompt: Duration of the degradation test at which the reported degradation extent was measured

Mass loss.prompt: Percentage mass loss or weight loss of the sample during degradation. Report the highest value reported for this material and test.

Molecular weight loss.prompt: Change in molecular weight during degradation, reported either as a percentage decrease or as the initial and final molecular weight

Degradation mechanism.prompt: Reported degradation mechanism, such as hydrolytic, enzymatic, oxidative, photodegradation, thermal, or microbial assimilation, including bulk or surface erosion when stated
Degradation mechanism.example: Bulk hydrolytic degradation followed by microbial assimilation

Degrading organisms or enzymes.prompt: Enzymes, microbial strains, or consortia used in or identified by the degradation test, with their source when reported

Biodegradation certification.prompt: Compostability or biodegradability certification or label reported for this material, such as TUV OK compost INDUSTRIAL, TUV OK compost HOME, OK biodegradable SOIL or MARINE, BPI certified, DIN CERTCO, or the Seedling logo

Type of study.prompt: Type of study (experimental, computational, or both)
